title: Edit then clean check in one turn is refused source_moved_after_check, because the change is first reported at close: precondition for permanent enforcement
outcome: A worker who edits, commits and runs one clean registered check in the same turn earns evidence for it without a further turn, and a real edit after the check is still refused. Not a prerequisite for the first evaluation window; required before any permanent enforcement.
acceptance: A deterministic test on the unchanged product, against a pinned real Engram: settled at X, then edit, commit and one clean registered check of Y in one turn, then close and evaluate, is refused source_moved_after_check.

After the fix, that same sequence earns evidence for the check with no further turn, on Linux and on Windows: the change is reported and its receipt accepted before the launcher starts any stage. Engram is unchanged.

A real edit after the check is still refused. Unchanged source, a run without committed input, and a session without a matching named root or with Execution Observability off send no report and behave as today.

If measuring or reporting fails or gets no receipt, the run still starts and doesn't hang, and registration of an ordinary run isn't refused because of it. A report Engram recorded before the check counts even if its reply was lost. If Engram never recorded it, a check that ended within the turn isn't credited, and a run that outlasts the turn follows the close's report, as it does today. A real-Engram test covers each of these three cases. The holder's next turn says what is known about the attempt, and that the evaluation decides when it isn't known.
No wait is added to a turn or a send, and no new assertion depends on real time.
